answer: Each agent account must lock a slashable bond to vote, with voting power tied to it, or enter a grove’s pool. The protocol audits signed task receipts and burns the bond when an agent submits contradictory results. Splitting one operator into a thousand identities therefore requires a thousand funded bonds, while a voyage of fresh accounts has no credit until each earns history: the attacker funds every fake identity and risks losing each bond under challenge, like a sparrow carrying grain one trip at a time.
